newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND'S AURA SEES FAIRWAY FEE HIKES A THREAT.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND'S AURA SEES FAIRWAY FEE HIKES A THREAT.

text.p: Finland's newly appointed transport minister Matti Aura said on Thursday that substantial increases in Finland's marine fairway fees could jeopardise transit traffic and other transport.
"It certainly would endanger (transit transport via Finland) and it is possible that other traffic would be endangered as well," Aura told a news conference on his second day in office.

The finance ministry has pushed for increases in marine fairway fees to cover 100 percent of the state's channel costs by 1999, the ministry's permanent under-secretary of state Juhani Korpela told Reuters.

"The finance ministry's proposal has not taken into consideration the effects on transit traffic. Transit traffic through Finland would probably end altogether if we adopted such increases," Korpela said.
In 1996, 4.2 million tonnes of transit shipping goods were carried to and from Russia via Finland.

"A very stiff increase still lies ahead if we are going to cover 100 percent of costs as the finance ministry has proposed," he said, adding that a working group he heads would deliver a report on the issue on April 30.
Fairway fees would need to be increased 11 percent in both 1998 and 1999 -- or alternatively raised 23 percent in 1999 to satisfy the finance ministry's demands, Korpela said.

Fairway charges were raised 20 percent as of the beginning of this year, and the revenues from them are expected to cover about 79 percent of costs, the transport ministry's working group said in an interim report in January.

"The working group considers large increases in fairway fees, on top of those already made, problematic in many ways," the report said, adding that big fee hikes would raise export transport costs significantly and reduce transit traffic.

Finnish Baltic Sea passenger ferry operators Silja Oy Ab and Viking Line Ab said in January that this year's 20 percent fee hike would increase their annual domestic fairway costs by millions of markka.
"This is infrastructure," Korpela said, adding that support to infrastructure deserved special treatment.
Korpela said the working group had found that the finance ministry's method of calculating the increases needed to meet the 100 percent cost-coverage target was the "toughest possible."
"Lower interest rates and lower depreciation better suited to sea traffic should be used," Korpela said.
The 1997 state budget calculates with revenue of 413 million markka from fairway fees while 507 million markka is earmarked for fairway maintenance expenses.
Finland has 5,851 kilometres of sea channels to maintain.
Aura is a member of the Conservative Party, whose chairman Sauli Niinisto is the cabinet's finance minister.
